key_insight: Neural model editing can be learned as a reinforcement learning problem, letting agents discover targeted weight updates that optimize task-specific edits while preserving overall model utility.
engineering_relevance: This offers a flexible alternative to hand-designed editing algorithms for applications like bias mitigation and machine unlearning in deployed neural systems.
method: Formulate model editing as RL with reward feedback.
Use MaskWorld for multiplicative weight scaling and ShiftWorld for additive weight shifts.
Combine utility-preservation and editing objectives in the reward signal.
evidence_signal: Across bias mitigation and unlearning benchmarks, the learned policies reduced forget-set accuracy to nearly 0% while keeping over 90% retain-set accuracy, and improved bias-related performance by more than 5% without losing general utility.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reward design and environment choice, so transfer to new architectures or editing goals may require careful tuning.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Neural Model Editing
